points: Q2 2026 revenue grew 20% reported and 16% constant-currency to $274.8 million, and management raised full-year 2026 guidance; the Q3 print will show whether that momentum is continuing as the $9.1 million FX tailwind from Brazil likely fades.

Adjusted EBITDA was $109.3 million in Q2, up 18% year over year, but margin dipped 50 bps to 39.8%; Q3 will reveal whether scale and cost control can stabilize or expand margin despite the ongoing Popular contract discount.

Adjusted EPS rose 18% to $1.05 in Q2, helped by buybacks; with consensus FY1 EPS near $4.00 and FY2 near $4.38, Q3 adjusted EPS growth needs to stay in the mid-to-high teens to keep the forward P/E 7.4 valuation gap intact.

The recently announced agreements with Transbank in Chile and Clip in Mexico are new growth avenues; Q3 commentary should indicate whether these partnerships are on track to contribute revenue in 2026.
The board increased the buyback authorization to $150 million after returning $50.1 million in Q2; Q3 disclosure of continued repurchases would support the lower share-count driver of EPS.

Peer prints from JKHY, PAYO and TOST just before EVTC may set sector tone, but EVTC's P/E discount to the theme and 10.4%/9.5% forward EPS growth give it a company-specific setup if it reaffirms or raises guidance.
watch: Constant-currency revenue growth at or above 16% year over year — supports the long.
Adjusted EBITDA margin holding near 39.8% or improving — supports the long.
Adjusted EPS growth in the mid-to-high teens year over year — supports the long.
Full-year 2026 revenue and adjusted EPS guidance maintained or raised — supports the long.
